tagline: A small river in a valley cut for a bigger one.
intro: The byway starts at Browns Valley, where a low divide parts Arctic water from Atlantic water. It picks up the Minnesota River where it leaves Big Stone Lake and follows it southeast through Montevideo and Granite Falls to New Ulm and Mankato, then northeast to Belle Plaine, some 300 miles of farm country and river towns.

The valley is too big for its river, up to five miles wide and 250 feet deep, cut by Glacial River Warren when Lake Agassiz drained. The flood scoured down to gneiss about 3.5 billion years old, quarried at Morton since the 1880s. The first battle of the U.S.-Dakota War of 1862 was fought on these banks.

moments.title: Lac qui Parle Mission
moments.text: At the lake which speaks, missionaries wrote the first dictionary of the Dakota language in the 19th century, and the WPA rebuilt the mission in 1942.

moments.title: Lower Sioux Agency
moments.text: The first organized battle of the war of 1862 was fought here on August 18. A stone warehouse of 1861 still stands, on ground the Lower Sioux Community now half owns.

moments.title: Hermann Heights Monument
moments.text: Over New Ulm a copper Hermann the German looks east with his sword raised, while St. Paul atop the cathedral nearby, also facing east, keeps his point planted in the ground.
